title: A signed snapshot reference always carries a real expiry: the Builder no longer defaults to "never", validate() refuses an unset or never expiring value, and the token parser no longer invents one

criteria.given: a SnapshotReference assembled with the Builder and never calling expiresAtEpochMillis(...)
criteria.then: the expiry field is the "unset" sentinel, not Long.MAX_VALUE, and signing is refused instead of minting a token that never expires

criteria.given: a reference whose expiry is unset (0), negative, or the old never-expires sentinel
criteria.then: validate() — called on both sign and verify — refuses it with "snapshot reference expiry is required"

criteria.given: a token payload with no 'e=' line, or one carrying e=9223372036854775807
criteria.then: it fails closed rather than defaulting to a permanent capability: the parser's sentinel is "unset" and the expiry guard decides

criteria.given: a reference with a real future expiry, and one whose expiry has already passed
criteria.then: the first still signs and verifies, and the second is still refused as expired — the change narrows nothing a legitimate reference relied on
